ca-tai-tuong-chien-xu-vinh-long.name: Vinh Long Crispy Whole Elephant Ear Fish
ca-tai-tuong-chien-xu-vinh-long.serving_basis: One fish of about 1 kg, served with greens, rice vermicelli and rice paper for four people.
ca-tai-tuong-chien-xu-vinh-long.description: The elephant ear fish is cleaned but left scaled, then deep-fried until the scales puff and crisp while the flesh stays tender. A signature Vinh Long dish, it is shared by wrapping the fish with rice paper, vermicelli, fresh herbs, starfruit and green banana.
ca-tai-tuong-chien-xu-vinh-long.finished_dish: The whole fish is golden and evenly crisp, with puffed scales; the flesh is moist, firm and fragrant rather than dry or burnt.
ca-tai-tuong-chien-xu-vinh-long.serving: Place the fish on a large platter. Pick off the flesh and wrap it with rice paper, vermicelli, herbs, starfruit and green banana. Serve with a sweet-sour garlic-chili fish sauce dip.
tips: Dry the fish thoroughly before frying to reduce splattering.
Use a deep pot and enough oil to submerge the fish; lower it in slowly once the oil is hot, then keep the heat moderate so it cooks through.
Use a food thermometer to check that the thickest flesh reaches at least 63°C; let the fish rest for about 3 minutes before serving.
ca-tai-tuong-chien-xu-vinh-long.image_alt: A whole golden, crispy elephant ear fish on a ceramic platter with herbs and starfruit.
ca-tai-tuong-chien-xu-vinh-long.time_note: About 70 minutes including a 15-minute salt-water soak; frying time depends on the fish size and oil temperature.
suggested_pairings: Fresh herbs, starfruit and green banana

ingredients.name: Green cooking banana

ingredients.notes: For the dipping sauce; adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Garlic

ingredients.name: Fresh chili

ingredients.name: Sugar

preparation_steps.instruction: Clean the gills and innards, leave the scales on, rinse quickly and soak the fish in lightly salted water for 15 minutes. Rinse again and pat the inside and outside completely dry.
Make shallow cuts across the thick parts of the fish without cutting through the fins or tail. Prepare the rice paper, vermicelli, washed herbs, starfruit and green banana.
Mix fish sauce with water, sugar and lime juice until the sugar dissolves. Add chopped garlic and chili, then taste and adjust.

cooking_steps.instruction: Pour enough oil into a deep pot to cover the fish and heat over medium. Test with a small piece; the oil should bubble steadily without smoking.

Using long tongs, lower the fish into the oil slowly. Fry until the scales puff and crisp and the fish is cooked through. Keep the heat moderate and adjust for the fish's size; avoid turning it repeatedly.
Lift the fish onto a rack over a tray and let it rest for 3 minutes. Check that the thickest part reaches at least 63°C, then serve whole with the herbs, vermicelli, rice paper and dipping sauce.

bo-nhung-me-buon-ma-thuot.name: Buon Ma Thuot Beef with Tamarind Sauce
aliases: Buon Ma Thuot beef dipped in tamarind sauce
bo-nhung-me-buon-ma-thuot.serving_basis: Four portions of thinly sliced beef dipped in hot tamarind sauce, served with greens and bread.
bo-nhung-me-buon-ma-thuot.description: Thin slices of beef are dipped in a gently bubbling, sweet-sour tamarind sauce with onion and a little butter. The Buon Ma Thuot serving style keeps the beef tender and fragrant; greens and bread balance the rich sauce.
bo-nhung-me-buon-ma-thuot.finished_dish: The tamarind sauce is lightly thick and balanced between sweet and sour; quickly dipped beef stays tender and the onion is softened but still crisp.
bo-nhung-me-buon-ma-thuot.serving: Set the hot pan of sauce in the middle of the table, with raw sliced beef on one side and watercress and bread on another. Dip a few slices at a time until just cooked; do not add all the beef at once.
tips: Slice the beef across the grain; chilling it briefly makes even thin slices easier.
Taste the sauce before dipping because tamarind and fish sauce vary in acidity and saltiness.
Only bring out the amount of raw beef needed for each round; keep it separate from washed greens and cooked food.
bo-nhung-me-buon-ma-thuot.image_alt: Thin slices of beef in a pan of sweet-sour tamarind sauce with onion and greens.
bo-nhung-me-buon-ma-thuot.time_note: About 60 minutes including 15 minutes to season the beef; dip each slice at the table to keep it tender.

ingredients.name: Ripe tamarind

ingredients.name: Fish sauce

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balance the tamarind's acidity.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Finely chop.

ingredients.name: Black pepper

preparation_steps.instruction: Soak the tamarind in warm water for 10 minutes, mash it and strain the pulp. Stir with water, fish sauce and sugar.
Slice the beef thinly across the grain. Lightly season with some chopped garlic, pepper and a teaspoon of fish sauce for 15 minutes; keep chilled.
Cut the onion into wedges, wash and drain the watercress, and warm the bread. Keep raw beef separate from washed greens and cooked foods.

cooking_steps.instruction: Heat a deep skillet or cast-iron pan, add the butter and coat the surface. Quickly saute the remaining garlic until fragrant.
Pour in the tamarind mixture, add the onion and bring to a gentle simmer. Taste and balance the sweet-sour flavor, keeping the pan gently bubbling.
At the table, dip a few slices of beef at a time until just cooked. Serve with watercress and bread; keep raw beef and its juices away from ready-to-eat food.

tep-dong-rang-khe.name: Field Shrimp Stir-Roasted with Starfruit
tep-dong-rang-khe.serving_basis: One plate of field shrimp with starfruit to share with rice among four people.
tep-dong-rang-khe.description: Small field shrimp are first roasted dry, then tossed with pork fat, shallots and sour starfruit. This rustic dish is nutty, lightly crisp and balanced between sour, salty and sweet, and is best served hot with white rice.
tep-dong-rang-khe.finished_dish: The shrimp are firm, lightly crisp and coral pink; the starfruit is softened but still holds its shape, with gentle sourness coating the shrimp.
tep-dong-rang-khe.serving: Spoon the shrimp and starfruit onto a plate, finish with scallions and pepper, and serve immediately with white rice and a light vegetable soup.
tips: Drain the shrimp well before roasting so they dry quickly and splatter less.
Add the starfruit after the shrimp have firmed up so it does not collapse or release too much liquid.
Add fish sauce gradually because tiny shrimp absorb seasoning quickly.
tep-dong-rang-khe.image_alt: A plate of field shrimp roasted with sour starfruit, scallions and black pepper.
tep-dong-rang-khe.time_note: About 35 minutes; dry-roast the shrimp before frying the shallots and seasoning.

ingredients.name: Fresh field shrimp
ingredients.notes: Trim long feelers, rinse well and drain.

ingredients.name: Sour starfruit

ingredients.name: Dried shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and finely chop.

ingredients.name: Pork fat

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season gradually to taste.

ingredients.name: Sugar

ingredients.name: Salt

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Sprinkle over the finished dish.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Wash and finely slice.

preparation_steps.instruction: Trim long feelers from the shrimp, rinse them several times and drain well. Trim the starfruit edges, rinse and cut into star-shaped slices.
Peel and chop the shallots; wash and slice the scallions. Measure the fish sauce, sugar and salt.

cooking_steps.instruction: Heat a pan and roast the shrimp, stirring, until the liquid evaporates and they turn pink and firm. Transfer them to a plate.
Add the pork fat to the pan and saute the shallots until fragrant. Return the shrimp, season with fish sauce, sugar and a little salt, then toss until coated.
When the shrimp have absorbed the seasoning, add the starfruit and toss briefly until just tender. Taste, finish with pepper and scallions, and turn off the heat.

canh-chua-ca-can-nam-o.name: Nam O Sour Reef-Fish Soup with Pineapple
aliases: Nam O sour fish soup with reef fish
canh-chua-ca-can-nam-o.serving_basis: One sour soup pot with about 500 g of local reef fish, served with rice for four people.
canh-chua-ca-can-nam-o.description: Fresh local reef fish is seasoned before cooking with pineapple, tomato and rice paddy herb. This Nam O fishing-village soup balances the firm sweetness of sea fish with the gentle sourness of pineapple and tomato and a touch of chili.
canh-chua-ca-can-nam-o.finished_dish: The broth is clear and lightly golden with a fresh sour finish; the local reef fish stays firm and intact, and the pineapple and tomato remain in pieces.
canh-chua-ca-can-nam-o.serving: Ladle the fish and broth into a serving bowl, then finish with rice paddy herb and cilantro. Serve hot with steamed rice and optional chili fish sauce.
tips: Choose fresh fish with clear eyes and firm flesh; clean it gently to avoid breaking the pieces.
Season the fish before adding it to gently boiling water, and avoid stirring so the pieces stay intact.
Adjust the sweet-sour seasoning after the fish is nearly cooked, as pineapple and tomato release liquid into the broth.
search_terms: Nam O fish soup with pineapple
canh-chua-ca-can-nam-o.image_alt: A bowl of Nam O sour local reef fish soup with cooked fish, pineapple, tomato and rice paddy herb.
canh-chua-ca-can-nam-o.time_note: About 70 minutes including a 20-minute fish marinade; simmer gently so the fish does not break apart.

preparation_steps.instruction: Clean the local reef fish, cut into pieces and drain. Marinate with some fish sauce, salt and pepper for 20 minutes.
Peel and slice the pineapple; cut the tomatoes into wedges. Wash and drain the rice paddy herb, cilantro and chili.

cooking_steps.instruction: Bring the water to a boil in a pot and add the crushed chili. Lower the heat to a gentle boil, then carefully add the fish.
Cook the fish for several minutes until the surface firms and skim any foam. Add pineapple and tomatoes; simmer gently until the fish is cooked.
Season with fish sauce, salt and sugar for a bright sweet-sour broth. Turn off the heat when the fish is firm and cooked, stir in rice paddy herb and cilantro, and serve hot.

mang-truc-yen-tu-xao-toi.name: Yen Tu Bamboo Shoots Stir-Fried with Garlic
aliases: Yen Tu garlic bamboo shoot side dish
mang-truc-yen-tu-xao-toi.serving_basis: One plate of garlic bamboo shoots as a vegetable side for four people.
mang-truc-yen-tu-xao-toi.description: Yen Tu bamboo shoots are cleaned and thoroughly boiled before a quick stir-fry with garlic and scallions. The side dish is tender-crisp and fragrant, allowing the shoots' natural sweetness to stand out. This is a meat-free vegetable side, distinct from the existing Yen Tu bamboo shoots stir-fried with beef.
mang-truc-yen-tu-xao-toi.finished_dish: The bamboo shoots are cooked through but still crisp, lightly seasoned, with pale-golden fragrant garlic and fresh green scallions.
mang-truc-yen-tu-xao-toi.serving: Serve hot as a separate vegetable side beside rice and a savory main. Use salt instead of fish sauce for a fully vegetarian meal.
tips: Boil fresh bamboo shoots in plenty of water, changing the water and cooking them thoroughly before stir-frying; do not eat unprocessed fresh shoots.
Drain the shoots well before adding them to a hot pan so they stir-fry rather than steam.
Season with fish sauce for a regular meal or salt for a vegetarian meal; add scallions at the end to keep their color.

Yen Tu bamboo shoots with garlic
mang-truc-yen-tu-xao-toi.image_alt: A plate of meat-free Yen Tu bamboo shoots stir-fried with garlic and scallions.
mang-truc-yen-tu-xao-toi.time_note: About 110 minutes including a one-hour soak; thoroughly boil the shoots and change the water before stir-frying.

ingredients.notes: Trim the tough base and damaged outer leaves; split or shred depending on size.

ingredients.name: Garlic

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Wash and finely slice.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For sauteing the garlic and bamboo shoots.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce or vegetarian soy sauce
ingredients.notes: Use vegetarian soy sauce or salt for a vegetarian meal.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: For boiling the bamboo shoots and seasoning.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Optional; softens the savory seasoning.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Lightly sprinkle at the end.

ingredients.name: Water

preparation_steps.instruction: Trim the tough base and damaged outer leaves, rinse the bamboo shoots and soak in rice-rinse water for about an hour if they taste bitter.
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil and cook the shoots thoroughly in at least two batches of fresh water. Drain, rinse and set aside.
Chop the garlic, wash and slice the scallions, and cut the bamboo shoots into bite-size pieces if needed.

cooking_steps.instruction: Heat the oil in a wide pan and saute most of the garlic until fragrant and pale gold, without browning it deeply.
Add the boiled, drained shoots and stir-fry over medium-high heat for 4–5 minutes until hot and the surface is dry.
Season with fish sauce or salt and optional sugar; toss until evenly coated. Add the remaining garlic, scallions and pepper, toss quickly and turn off the heat.
